title: FloodGuard planning protocol v1b: engineering addendum
status_note: Draft for signature, written by an AI coding agent. Agents draft, humans sign. Nothing in this file is in force. Every open item is closed and every parameter it names is filled in; the schema refuses this status otherwise. The owners approved this file in principle (decision-log entry R11) and approved all 23 owner choices of docs/proposal_execution/planning_protocol_v1b_owner_choices.md exactly as recommended (decision-log entry R12, 3 October 2026); neither is a signature. The last four items (OI-01, OI-03, OI-04 and OI-06) were closed on 3 October 2026 from the run of record of the chosen corridor, made in a compute window that the agent declared under R12 (corridor_polygon.run_of_record). The drafter readings still await confirmation: the signers mark them in the signing edit, after reading the closures (docs/proposal_execution/planning_protocol_v1b_closures_summary.md). Until the signed file's SHA-256 is recorded in docs/proposal_execution/RECEIPTS.jsonl, no FPPS, no A-E class and no ensemble may be computed for any real unit. No receipt has been written.

route_selection_rule.status: Decided by the owners on 3 October 2026 (decision log R12, owner choice 1, option B as written, with its seven sub-rules, as recommended). Not in the plan: plan 1.1's words 'trunk and primary routes' become 'fastest routes'.
route_selection_rule.rule: For each of the three hospitals: build an undirected vehicle graph from every OSM road in the search window that lies inside Thailand, joining ways wherever they share a vertex coordinate; use the modelled class speeds; snap the hospital to the road vertex nearest to its OSM way polygon; take the fastest path from that vertex to the first road vertex inside AOI-02 (the vertex of AOI-02 with the smallest travel time); keep every segment of that path, whatever its road class; buffer the path by 3 km in EPSG:32647; and union the three buffers with AOI-02.
sub_rules: 1. Where the path ends: at the road vertex inside AOI-02 that is quickest to reach from the hospital; not at Mae Sai town, not at a tambon centre.

2. The route graph ignores grade: ways are joined wherever they share a vertex coordinate, whatever their bridge, tunnel or layer tags. The routing context does not do that (grade_join_policy), so the route search can pass a junction that the context later treats as apart.
3. Thailand only: roads in Myanmar and Laos are not used, even where they are shorter.
4. Search window: the bounding box of AOI-02 widened by 0.45 degrees on each side (99.36-100.49 E, 19.81-20.92 N). A faster route that leaves this box would not be found.

5. Speeds: the fixed class speeds of evidence_scenarios.py (motorway 80, trunk 70, primary 60, secondary 50, tertiary 40, residential and unclassified 25, local 20 km/h). Undirected: one-way rules and turn restrictions are not modelled.
6. Excluded roads: ways tagged access or motor_vehicle = no or private.
7. Hospital snap: the nearest road vertex to the hospital's OSM polygon; the snap distances were 0 m, 0 m and 4 m.
route_selection_rule.proposal: For each of the three hospitals, take the baseline fastest vehicle path on the national OSM graph from the AOI-02 boundary to the hospital way, keep its trunk and primary segments (including links), buffer them by 3 km and union the result with AOI-02. Record the path edge IDs.

closure_rule_v1.geometry: Each edge is the straight segment between its two nodes, projected to EPSG:32647. Intersected length is the length of that segment inside the flood extent. Intersected fraction f is min(1, intersected length / segment length). This is the measurement used in src/floodguard/evidence_flood_scenario.py.
closure_rule_v1.geometry_status: Drafter reading DR-B02. The plan does not say how intersected length is measured or what counts as 'any intersection'. Both are taken from src/floodguard/evidence_flood_scenario.py (straight node-to-node segment in EPSG:32647; an edge is intersected when the length inside the extent is greater than 1e-6 m), so that the permissive regression can match the finals closed-edge IDs exactly. The owners confirm at signing.

central.closed_when: f >= 0.5 OR intersected length >= L(road class); bridges and culverts close at f >= 0.25

permissive.closed_when: any intersection: intersected length > 1e-6 m, the threshold in src/floodguard/evidence_flood_scenario.py that the regression must reproduce
permissive.note: Under this level no intersected edge stays open, so the delay factor has no effect.

closure_rule_v1.delay_factor_pairing_status: Drafter reading DR-B01. The other reading, k as a separate three-level axis, would give 1,620 cells. The owners confirm at signing.

trigger_B_isolation.definition: A top-20 link of the case's baseline critical-link ranking that intersects the flood extent is closed on its own. The trigger fires when at least 500 of the unit's residents who had a baseline vehicle route to a hospital or a main-road entry lose every such route.

trigger_C_serving_facility.definition: A facility serves a unit when it is the baseline-nearest facility of its kind, by vehicle travel time, for at least 100 of the unit's residents. The 100 is tied to guardrail GR1, which already uses 100 residents as the smallest group the protocol says anything about: a reuse of a signed number, not evidence. 'Inside the extent' means the facility point, or the centroid of its footprint, is inside the flood extent. 'Uniquely located' follows facility_sets.shelter_location_rule.

rules: While status is incomplete_draft, open items are closed by editing this file. In one edit: fill in every parameter the item lists in parameter_pointers, set the item's status to closed and add its closure (the value, the producing run and its receipt or output SHA-256).

An owner answer recorded in the decision log may be written into its slots before the rest of an item is produced. The item then stays open and lists the filled slots under owner_answer, with the answer, what is still needed and the SHA-256 of the decision-log line. It closes, in one edit, when its remaining parameters are filled.
A closed item with an empty parameter is refused by the tests, and a file with status draft_for_signature or signed that has an empty parameter is refused by the schema.
When every open item is closed and every section's status is fixed, the status becomes draft_for_signature, and the signers may amend and sign.

At signing, every entry in drafter_readings is set to confirmed or amended. An amended entry is also listed in signature_block.amendments_at_signing, and the parameter it points to is edited to match.
After the signed file's SHA-256 is recorded in RECEIPTS.jsonl, this file is not edited again.
Any later change needs planning_protocol_v2 with a written reason. Every run is reported.
